newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Thwarting pre-Christmas holiday fever, South African shares set new record turnover on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange of 1.07 billion rand, including a large overnight asset swap, dealers said.
The previous record was 999.7 million rand on April 6, 1996.
Dealers said a large asset swap took place on Wednesday night, contributing about 300 million rand to overall turnover.
"Trade was very active today with over a billion rand of shares trading. There was an asset swap on the all-shares which was about 300 million rand," a dealer said.
But, despite shrugging off Wall Street's heavy losses and stifling their morning drop, industrials and all-shares finished the day weak as a falling rand took its toll.

"Wall Street didn't really affect stocks. Most of the losses were already discounted. But the negative effect came from the rand later. Then gilts fell out of bed and this, combined with a worsening money market shortage, all took its toll on the equity market," a dealer said.
The rand lost nearly nine cents of its value on the day, pulled down by dollar demand out of London and then strong local importer demand, "catching some people sleeping", dealers said.
Gold shares remained stuck in their tight range and dipped to close slightly weaker as a listless bullion price failed to move them.

Overall, dealers were looking for a firmer market on Friday. They said unit-trusts would start window-dressing stocks and that futures players would want to close off a lot of open reverse arbitrage positions ahead of the close-out on Tuesday.
"We're looking at a stronger market tomorrow. But the futures players are the name of the game. They've got a bunch of reverse arbs they want shutting," a dealer said.
Industrials ended 37.1 points down at 7,814.7, all-shares were off 32.1 at 6,607 and golds dipped 8.9 to 1,533.2.
Gold Fields lost 850 cents to 130 rand, Duiker added 50 cents to 11.80 rand and Lonrho added 16 cents to 942 cents.

Near-term industrial equity index futures firmed from the start of trade on Thursday in the wake of Wednesday's frail show and despite a slide of more than 70 points on Wall Street overnight, which dealers said was largely discounted.
Industrial futures then slipped to around settlement levels as players tried to push spot higher, but finished a tad firmer.
The December industrial contract was at 7,500/10 from 7,495, the all gold was at 1,065/71 from 1,072 and the all-share was bid at 6,015 from 6,025.
